name: Sereja and Intervals
description: Sereja is interested in intervals of numbers, so he has prepared a problem about intervals for you. An interval of numbers is a pair of integers [ l , r ] (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ m ) . Interval [ l 1 , r 1 ] belongs to interval [ l 2 , r 2 ] if the following condition is met: l 2 ≤ l 1 ≤ r 1 ≤ r 2 . Sereja wants to write out a sequence of n intervals [ l 1 , r 1 ] , [ l 2 , r 2 ] , ... , [ l n , r n ] on a piece of paper. At that, no interval in the sequence can belong to some other interval of the sequence. Also, Sereja loves number x very much and he wants some (at least one) interval in the sequence to have l i = x . Sereja wonders, how many distinct ways to write such intervals are there? Help Sereja and find the required number of ways modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) . Two ways are considered distinct if there is such j (1 ≤ j ≤ n ) , that the j -th intervals in two corresponding sequences are not equal.
input_specification: The first line contains integers n , m , x (1 ≤ n · m ≤ 100000, 1 ≤ x ≤ m ) — the number of segments in the sequence, the constraints on the numbers in segments and Sereja's favourite number.
output_specification: In a single line print the answer modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) .
subsubtopic: 461. Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
approach_summary: Iterate over interval length len from 1 to N and left endpoint l. Transition by splitting at midpoint k: dp[l][r] = min/max_k (dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + cost) in O(N^3).

topic_editorial.summary: Interval / Range Dynamic Programming by interval length.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The problem satisfies interval substructure: the optimal cost for range $[l, r]$ depends on splitting into subsegments $[l, k]$ and $[k+1, r]$ for some pivot $k \in [l, r-1]$. Computing shorter intervals first ensures that all subproblems are ready when evaluating longer intervals.
